standard_prerequisites.statement: The Cauchy reals embed into the Dedekind reals.
standard_prerequisites.use: It reduces the goal to showing that every Dedekind real is merely a limit of a Cauchy sequence at source line 1818.

standard_prerequisites.name: Cauchy sequence of rationals
standard_prerequisites.statement: A Cauchy sequence of rationals converges to a real when the terms approximate it arbitrarily well.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the object constructed by the recursion in the proof.

core_obligations: Note that the assumed type is an untruncated variant of the weak linearity statement for the order, cited as the retained equation (source lines 1816-1817).
Use the embedding of the Cauchy reals into the Dedekind reals to reduce the goal to showing that every Dedekind real is merely a limit of a Cauchy sequence of rationals (source lines 1818-1819).

From the assumption and the inhabitation of cuts obtain a, b : Q with a < x < b, and build a sequence of nested rational intervals by recursion: start at (a,b) and, at each step, trisect and use c(s,t) to decide which half to keep (source lines 1821-1832).
Show that the endpoints satisfy q_n < x < r_n and that the widths shrink by the factor 2/3 at each step, so that both endpoint sequences are Cauchy and converge to the cut x (source lines 1834-1838).

proof_roadmap.step: Identify the assumption and reduce to approximating Dedekind reals by Cauchy sequences.
Build the nested trisection sequence using the assumed choice function.
Verify the width estimate and conclude convergence.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is Lemma 11.4.1 at source lines 1803-1813: if every Dedekind real merely carries an untruncated linearity function for the order, then the Cauchy and Dedekind reals coincide. The author's proof (source lines 1815-1839) is a construction rather than a citation: after recognising the assumption as an untruncated form of weak linearity (lines 1816-1817) and reducing to approximating Dedekind reals by Cauchy sequences of rationals (lines 1818-1819), it builds a nested sequence of rational intervals by repeated trisection in which the assumed function decides which subinterval still contains the cut (lines 1821-1832), and then verifies both the containment q_n < x < r_n and the geometric width estimate before concluding that the two endpoint sequences converge to x (lines 1834-1838). The statement is a one-line implication and hides the whole trisection construction.
